defaults.permitted_development: A rear extension can be permitted development in England if it stays within the Class A depth, height and curtilage limits for the house. Larger single-storey rear additions can sometimes go further, but only through the prior-approval route. On deeper rural plots, the harder issues are often prominence in open views, out-of-scale massing and how the addition reads from lanes or public footpaths.

rules.height_rules: Single-storey rear extensions should stay within the 4m overall height limit, with eaves no higher than 3m if any part is within 2m of a boundary. Two-storey rear work must not exceed the existing house height or eaves.
rules.depth_rules: Standard single-storey rear extensions can usually project up to 3m on a semi-detached or terraced house and 4m on a detached house. The larger home extension route can extend that to 6m or 8m with prior approval. Two-storey rear extensions should normally project no more than 3m.
rules.boundary_rules: Where any part sits within 2m of a boundary, eaves height becomes especially sensitive, and two-storey rear extensions also need enough rear-boundary separation to avoid overbearing and overlooking problems. On deeper rural plots, the harder issues are often prominence in open views, out-of-scale massing and how the addition reads from lanes or public footpaths.
rules.roof_rules: The roof should remain subordinate to the original house. Balconies, verandas and raised platforms are not part of the normal rear-extension permitted development route.
rules.materials_rules: External materials should be similar in appearance to the existing house so the extension reads as a planned addition rather than an unrelated rear block. On deeper rural plots, the harder issues are often prominence in open views, out-of-scale massing and how the addition reads from lanes or public footpaths.

rules.permitted_development: A rear extension can still fall within Class A in England, but in parts of this authority heritage controls or an Article 4 direction may narrow that fallback route. Even where rights remain, the depth, height and curtilage limits still apply.

rules.height_rules: The same height rules apply in sensitive areas: 4m overall for single-storey rear work, 3m eaves within 2m of a boundary, and no rear upper floor that overtops the existing house or eaves.
rules.depth_rules: Standard single-storey rear extensions can usually project up to 3m on a semi or terraced house and 4m on a detached house, with the larger home extension prior-approval route going further in some cases. Two-storey rear extensions are much tighter and should normally project no more than 3m.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary privacy and bulk are usually judged more tightly in sensitive streets. The near-boundary eaves rule still applies, and upper floors need enough separation from the rear boundary to avoid overlooking and dominance.
rules.roof_rules: The roof should remain subordinate to the original house. Balconies, verandas and raised platforms are not part of the normal rear-extension permitted development route.
rules.materials_rules: Close material matching matters even more in heritage-sensitive settings so the rear addition reads as a restrained extension of the existing house.
